meta.subtitle: VYJUVEK grows 24% at a 95% gross margin; the fourth-quarter IOLITE readout and European pricing decide whether the multiple holds

analystSentiment.commentary:
Krystal Biotech is a one-product commercial company that already earns like a mature franchise. VYJUVEK brought in $119.2M in Q2'26 at a 95% gross margin, and quarterly net income was $54.8M. The question for the stock is not whether the business is good but how much of the next year is already in a $322.28 share price.

We rate the shares HOLD with a $300–$390 target range over a horizon running into early 2027, after the fourth-quarter readouts. Our Base case has the market keep its current forward multiple as FY27 becomes the forward year; the Valuation section sets out how each scenario is anchored. That Base sits above today's price, but the Bear case is deep enough that the probability-weighted value offers only modest upside.

The case for patience rather than buying is concentration. VYJUVEK is the whole revenue line, growth is running below the pace consensus needs (see Financials), and the near-term pipeline value rests on one small eye-drop trial.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
Krystal Biotech, Inc. is a Pittsburgh-based, commercial-stage genetic medicines company built on an engineered HSV-1 vector platform. Its only commercial product, VYJUVEK, is a topical, redosable gene therapy for dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa (DEB), approved in the United States, the EU, Japan and, since May 2026, the UK. The company reports a single segment, and VYJUVEK has generated $965.9M in cumulative net product revenue since its 2023 U.S. launch.

The pipeline uses the same vector across the eye (KB803, KB801), lung (KB407, KB408, inhaled KB707), skin (KB111) and aesthetics (KB304). Two programs, KB803 and KB801, are in studies the company calls registrational. Nothing in the pipeline is yet approved, so today's earnings are VYJUVEK's earnings.

thesis.label: HOLD
thesis.body:
VYJUVEK alone already supports most of the share price: Q2'26 revenue grew {+ 24% +} with an operating margin of 49%, and the balance sheet carries no funding need we can see. If consensus earnings arrive and the multiple holds, the stock has room to rise into early 2027.

The counter-case is that growth is slowing, European prices are still pending, and the pipeline's nearest value event is a 16-patient registrational trial. A miss on those fronts could take the stock back toward the low end of its 52-week range. Weighing both, we see the shares as fairly priced for a HOLD rather than a BUY.

catalysts: KB803 IOLITE top-line results, guided for 4Q 2026 as of the August 3, 2026 results; see Growth.
VYJUVEK launches in Italy and Spain, which the August 3, 2026 press release expected before year end; the 10-Q frames them as potential launches that depend on pricing. See Growth.
Completion of EMERALD-1 enrollment for KB801 and FDA alignment on the KB407 registrational design, both guided for late 2026 as of August 3, 2026.
risks: Single-product dependence on VYJUVEK; see Risks.
Growth deceleration against a consensus that needs a stronger second half; see Financials.
Pipeline timelines have already slipped once this year; see Management.

income.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.incomeCommentary:
The income statement has turned from losses to high margins in three years. Diluted EPS went from a loss of $5.49 per share in FY22 to positive results of 0.39 in FY23, 3.00 in FY24 and 6.84 in FY25, while operating margin moved from a negative 216.2% in FY23 to 22.6% in FY24 and 41.5% in FY25. FY25 revenue was $389.1M, {+ up 33.9% +}.

The Q2'26 quarter kept the margin story intact. Product revenue was $119.2M against $96.0M a year earlier, cost of goods sold fell to $6.4M from $7.2M, and gross margin was 95%. R&D was flat at $14.5M against $14.4M, while SG&A rose to $39.9M from $35.1M, so operating leverage came mainly from the revenue line. Diluted EPS was $1.79 against $1.29.

Two cautions. First, growth is slowing: Q2'26 revenue rose {+ 24.1% +}, below the FY25 pace and below the ~31% growth embedded in the FY26E consensus of $511.1M. First-half revenue was $235.6M, so consensus implies second-half revenue well above that figure; the Italy and Spain launches would help, but European prices are still pending (see Risks). Second, TTM net margin of 54.8% sits above the 44.9% operating margin; the facts here do not say why, so we do not treat the gap as recurring. Consensus EPS basis is unstated, while reported EPS is GAAP and includes stock-based compensation of $11.7M in Q2'26 SG&A alone, so the forward multiples in Valuation should not be read as GAAP-based.

balance.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.balanceCommentary:
The balance sheet is a strength. The vendor's cash and short-term investments rose in each year from FY22 to FY25, reaching $0.8B at FY25. The Q2'26 press release reports $1.1 billion of cash, cash equivalents and investments at June 30, 2026. The two figures are on different bases, since the company's measure can include investments the vendor line excludes, so we do not read the gap as a six-month cash build; we use the company's figure for the current position. Total equity reached $1.2B in FY25.

The vendor table carries no debt figures ("—"), which we treat as missing data rather than as zero; the excerpts in Context do not describe any borrowing either. The TTM current ratio is 8.32, below the levels above 13 recorded in FY21–FY23 but still high. On that evidence Krystal looks able to fund its disclosed programs, including the registrational starts guided for 2027, without new equity. The counter-point is that a large cash balance only helps holders if it is spent well; capital allocation is discussed under Management.

cashflow.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.cashflowCommentary:
Cash generation now tracks earnings. FY25 free cash flow was $188.9M, a 48.5% FCF margin, up from 41.0% in FY24, with capital expenditure of $12M. Operating cash flow and free cash flow have both been positive only since FY24; FY21–FY23 were cash-consuming years.

At today's price the FCF yield is 2.7%, which is thin for a single-product company and means most of the valuation rests on growth rather than current cash returns. The company pays no dividend, and the vendor reports no repurchase figures. Management's FY 2026 guidance for non-GAAP R&D and SG&A combined is $175.0 - $195.0 million, excluding stock-based compensation, which the company says it cannot estimate. Spending within that range against a revenue base heading toward consensus would keep free cash flow rising; a step-up in registrational spending in 2027 is the main reason it might not.

multiples.note: Peer multiples pending a peer data source.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
On trailing numbers the stock is priced at 40.4x earnings, 43.7x EV/EBITDA and 21.7x sales. On forward numbers the vendor gives two figures that disagree: ~34.6x on FY27E EPS in the snapshot and 41.0x on an NTM basis in the multiples table. We use the NTM figure for the Base case because it is the multiple the market applies to the year ahead, and that year rolls into FY27 within our horizon.

No peer multiples are available, so the read is absolute. A multiple near 40x for a business with a 95% gross margin and roughly half of revenue converting to free cash flow is not extreme, but it leaves no room for VYJUVEK growth to stall. The Street's consensus target of $392.11 and median of $400.00 sit above our Base, and its $284.00 low sits well above our Bear, so our call is more cautious than the 11 Buy ratings imply.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: IOLITE reads out positively in 4Q 2026, Italy and Spain launch on schedule, and EMERALD-1 completes enrollment. The market starts paying for a second product, and the stock reaches the Street's high target of $474.00.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: VYJUVEK stays on track for consensus FY27E EPS of $9.32, and by early 2027, when FY27 becomes the forward year, the market keeps paying the current 41.0x NTM multiple on it. Pipeline readouts are mixed and add little.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: IOLITE misses, European prices settle below launch levels and VYJUVEK growth keeps slowing, so earnings stall near FY26E EPS of $7.87. The market stops paying a growth multiple and the stock returns to about its 52-week low of $179.16.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
Each scenario has a checkable anchor over a horizon running into early 2027. Base applies the vendor's NTM multiple to FY27E consensus EPS, on the view that once FY27 is the year ahead the market pays what it pays today for the year ahead. Bear uses the stock's own 52-week low, a level it traded at within the past year, because a stalled single-product company would lose the growth premium rather than keep a forward multiple in the mid-30s. Bull uses the Street's high target.

We weight Base at 55%, Bear at 25% and Bull at 20%. Bear gets the larger tail because its ingredients are already partly visible: growth is below the consensus pace and European pricing is unsettled, so an IOLITE miss would land on a slowing story. Bull needs several things to go right at once, a positive readout from a 16-patient trial plus on-time launches and enrollment. The Bear tail is also wider in dollars than the Bull tail, so the probability-weighted fair value sits well below Base and only modestly above today's price. That expected upside, set against a deep Bear downside, gives a HOLD.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Krystal reports one segment, and all FY25 revenue of $389.1M came from VYJUVEK net product sales. The company sells directly in the United States, major European markets and Japan, and is building a specialty distributor network elsewhere. The vendor data carry no geographic split, so we do not quote one. Pricing was completed in Japan before launch; the status of European pricing is covered under Risks.

moatFactors.name: First corrective therapy in DEB
moatFactors.body: The Q2'26 10-Q describes VYJUVEK as "the first and only corrective medicine approved by the FDA for the treatment of both recessive and dominant subtypes of DEB," and says it is "the first and only corrective therapy approved for the treatment of DEB" in Japan, the EU and the UK. The broadened U.S. label discussed under Growth reinforces that position. The limit is that this protects one indication in a rare disease, not a broad franchise.

moatFactors.name: Biologic exclusivity
moatFactors.body: The 2025 10-K describes a 12-year period before a biosimilar approval can take effect after a reference product's first FDA licensure. The same risk factor warns that a competitor can still win approval during that window with its own full BLA, that the period could be shortened by congressional action, and that recent FDA draft guidance could lower the burden for biosimilars. We treat exclusivity as real but not absolute.

moatFactors.name: Commercial and manufacturing footprint
moatFactors.body: The company runs two in-house, commercial scale CGMP manufacturing facilities and, per the Q2'26 press release, has secured over 730 reimbursement approvals and over 640 unique prescribers for VYJUVEK. That base takes time for a newcomer to rebuild. It is still a footprint in one disease, and it does not transfer automatically to the eye, lung or skin programs.

moatFactors.name: Vector platform
moatFactors.body: In October 2025 the FDA granted platform technology designation to the HSV-1 vector used in KB801, which the 10-Q says affords development and manufacturing efficiencies. This is a potential advantage across the pipeline, but it has not yet produced a second approval.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat NARROW. VYJUVEK's position in DEB looks durable over the next several years, supported by its approval status in four jurisdictions and the reimbursement base, though exclusivity is not absolute (see the factor above). The moat does not extend beyond one rare-disease indication today. A positive IOLITE readout would extend the franchise within DEB rather than widen it into new diseases; a KB801 approval would be an early test of whether the platform designation turns into a broader advantage.

points: VYJUVEK geographic expansion: launched in Germany in August 2025 and in France and Japan in October 2025, approved in the UK in May 2026, and, as of the August 3, 2026 results, expected to launch in Italy and Spain before year end, with marketing authorization applications for Switzerland and Australia planned for 2H 2026. The 10-Q is more conditional, calling Italy and Spain potential launches whose timing depends on pricing negotiations. The counter-case is price: European revenue per patient is not yet settled (see Risks).

U.S. depth: the September 2025 label update opened treatment from birth and home application, and the company reports growing use of VYJUVEK as a lifelong wound management therapy. The facts do not split U.S. from international revenue, so we cannot confirm how much of the {+ 24% +} Q2'26 growth came from the U.S.

KB803 (IOLITE): a registrational, placebo-controlled crossover study in DEB patients with corneal abrasions, fully enrolled in April 2026 with 16 patients, top-line results guided for 4Q 2026. The 10-Q says ocular complications are thought to affect over 25% of DEB patients and that no corrective therapy is available. The evidence beyond IOLITE is a single compassionate-use case, so we do not assume a positive readout.

KB801 (EMERALD-1) for neurotrophic keratitis: a registrational study of approximately 60 patients, with enrollment guided as of August 3, 2026 to complete before year end. This would give Krystal a product outside DEB; recombinant NGF eye drops are already approved for NK, so KB801 would compete on dosing burden rather than enter an empty market.

Later-stage optionality: KB407 in cystic fibrosis (FDA alignment on a registrational design expected in 4Q 2026, study start in 2027), KB111 in Hailey-Hailey disease (registrational start targeted for 2027) and inhaled KB707 in NSCLC (31% ORR with pembrolizumab in a late-line Phase 1/2 cohort, registrational plans in 1H 2027). These are early and contribute little to our Base case.

management.leadership:
Per the April 3, 2026 proxy, the 2025 named executive officers were Krish S. Krishnan, Chairman of the Board and Chief Executive Officer; Suma M. Krishnan, Founder and President; and Kathryn A. Romano, Executive Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer. The proxy excerpt carries no tenure or background detail, so we do not add any.

Execution on VYJUVEK has been strong: approvals in four jurisdictions and a profitable launch. Pipeline timing is less reliable. The April 2026 proxy said the company had the potential to initiate registrational programs in cystic fibrosis and Hailey-Hailey disease later in 2026; the August 2026 press release now targets 2027 for both. The documents do not give a reason for the change. We read it as a modest credibility cost, not a red flag, and the 4Q 2026 KB407 FDA alignment is the date to hold management to.
management.capitalAllocation:
Capital so far has gone to R&D, the commercial build-out and in-house manufacturing; the company pays no dividend and the vendor reports no buyback figures. The FY 2026 non-GAAP opex guidance in Financials keeps spending disciplined relative to revenue.

The open question is the use of a cash balance that keeps growing. Management is funding several registrational programs and a separate aesthetics subsidiary, Jeune Aesthetics, which plans a Phase 2 KB304 study in 2027. Aesthetics is a different market from rare disease, and the filings in Context do not explain its expected economics. We would prefer to see cash spent on the eye and lung programs first; any large acquisition or a step-up in aesthetics spending would weaken the case.
management.governance:
Per the April 3, 2026 proxy, the Board determined that six current directors (Messrs. Gangolli, Janney and Rossi, Drs. Mason and Sutherland, and Ms. Mazzacco) and former director Mr. Ganorkar are independent under Nasdaq standards. The excerpt does not give the total board size, so we cannot state the independent share. Krish S. Krishnan is both Chairman and CEO, Suma M. Krishnan, the Founder and President, is also a named executive officer, and the excerpt does not mention a lead independent director.

For outside holders, that structure means the executive who proposes how the growing cash balance is spent, including on aesthetics, also leads the board that approves it. The independent directors and the three standing committees are the check, and the Audit Committee must approve related-party transactions above $120,000 under the proxy's written policy; the excerpt discloses no specific transactions. We see this as a reason to hold management to the capital-allocation tests set out above rather than as a red flag.
management.insiderOwnership: The proxy excerpt in Context does not include the beneficial ownership table, so we cannot state what share of Krystal the executives, the founder or any 5% holder owns. Such holder figures typically come from the holders' own 13G filings, and none were captured. Without that data we make no claim about insider control; the governance view above rests on board structure alone.

idiosyncratic: Product concentration: VYJUVEK is Krystal's sole commercial product, and the 2025 10-K states that near-term prospects and future growth are substantially dependent on its commercial success. Any safety signal, supply interruption or slowdown in U.S. demand would hit the entire revenue line. Watch quarterly VYJUVEK revenue growth against the Q2'26 pace.

European pricing: the company is selling in Germany and France ahead of final prices, with negotiations expected, as of August 3, 2026, to run until at least 2H 2026 in Germany and into 2027 in France; Italy, Spain and the UK are still in discussion. A final price below the launch level would lower revenue per patient in those markets. Watch the German outcome and the Italy and Spain launch prices.

IOLITE readout: the company modified the KB803 dosing schedule after observing what it calls a promising safety profile in the initial patients, to reduce the potential impact of human error in eye drop administration. Even so, 16 patients enrolled under the updated protocol is a small base for a registrational result, and a miss would remove the nearest extension of the DEB franchise. Watch the 4Q 2026 top-line release, including the primary endpoint versus placebo.

Competitive entry: a rival approved through its own BLA, as the moat discussion describes, would pressure price and share in DEB. Watch for competing DEB filings and the finalization of FDA biosimilar guidance.

Pipeline slippage: further delays beyond those described under Management would push any second revenue stream out and weaken the Bull case; KB408 interim results are already not due until 2027. Watch the 4Q 2026 KB407 FDA alignment and the 2027 study starts.
risks.systemic: In our view the broader risks are those of any U.S. rare-disease drug company: pricing and reimbursement policy and FDA policy toward gene therapies, neither of which the excerpts in Context quantify. The stock's 52-week range shows how far sentiment can swing. The excerpts describe no borrowing, so on that evidence rate and credit conditions matter mainly through the multiple the market will pay rather than through funding, though the vendor's debt fields are blank rather than zero.

body: We rate Krystal Biotech HOLD with a $300–$390 target range against a $322.28 price. VYJUVEK's profitability is not in doubt; the issue is that a Base case near the 52-week high is balanced by a Bear case near the 52-week low, and the weighted value sits only modestly above the current price.

What would change the call: a positive IOLITE readout with clean European pricing would shift weight toward the Bull case and move us to BUY. A weak IOLITE readout combined with Q3'26 or Q4'26 VYJUVEK growth below the Q2'26 pace would point to the Bear path and move us toward SELL.
